newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK monetary meeting today.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK monetary meeting today.

text.p: Following is a list of analysts' reactions to the surprise news the UK Treasury had brought Wednesday's monthly monetary meeting forward to 0700 GMT this morning.
The meeting will be the first since Gordon Brown took over as Chancellor of the Exchequer on Friday, after the landslide victory for the Labour Party in Thursday's election.
British official interest rates are currently at 6.0 percent. -

CIBC CHIEF ECONOMIST DAVID COLEMAN - "I think they're going to announce a 25 basis point increase in base rates. It's good PR with the markets. There's been a lot of talk that he (Brown) might try to delay the meeting, take some time to be briefed and get his feet under the table. So the fact he's actually brought the meeting forward suggests completely the opposite. It shows he's willing to make tough decision. From a credibility perspective it's very encouraging. It will probably be the easiest rate increase he'll ever get to make."

IAN GUNNER, ECONOMIST AT CHASE INVESTMENT BANK - "It looks like we're going to get a quarter-point rate rise, and it will probably be announced at 1000 GMT...The change in timing suggests Brown is keen to make a forceful move and take the initiative. This should be good for the markets and positive for sterling."

ROYAL BANK OF SCOTLAND ECONOMIST NEIL PARKER - "Most forecast a rate increase of 25 basis points and we forecast a 50 basis point rise. If our forecasts are realised, then we could see a marked negative move in short sterling and a positive move in sterling. We don't forecast this to last since this is the necessary inflationary fix for past policy mistakes."
